final_answer: imagine a small town where every time the church bell rings, a nearby bakery sells more cookies. a curious resident might think, "the bell must cause people to buy cookies!" but wait—what if the bell rings every morning at 8 am, when people start their day and naturally stop by the bakery for a snack? the real cause is the time of day, not the bell itself. this shows correlation (bell rings and cookie sales rise) doesn’t mean causation (bell causing sales). the hidden variable here is the routine of daily life. just because two things happen together doesn’t mean one caused the other—there might be a third factor at play.
